tweets: It took the Chandela dynasty roughly 200 years to raise 85 temples in the heart of India. Then history forgot them - swallowed by jungle for 700 years.

Between the 9th and 12th centuries, Chandela kings turned Khajuraho, in today's Madhya Pradesh, into a temple city. Builders stacked massive sandstone blocks with no mortar - precision joints and sheer weight held every wall up.

Every outer wall is carved edge to edge: gods, goddesses, elephants, dancers, musicians, warriors, scenes of daily life - thousands of figures caught mid-motion. Few sites on Earth pack this much stone sculpture into one place.
By the 1200s the Chandela dynasty had faded and the temples were left behind. Dense forest crept in, hiding the roughly 20 that survived from most of the world for centuries.

In 1838, British engineer T.S. Burt was led to the ruins by local villagers who had never forgotten them. Today Khajuraho is a UNESCO World Heritage Site - two centuries of ambition, uncovered. Follow @yddoseOfHistory for your daily dose of history.
